title: The Exiled Princes
subtitle: The opening scene of one Lithuanian-labeled tale

exile.excerpt: There was once a King who had three sons, and he had also a stepdaughter. They all lived together in peace and happiness and had everything their hearts could desire. But after a time an enemy of the King came against him with a great army, and slew him, and took the kingdom and drove forth the Princes into the world, and their stepsister with them.
exile.note: Verbatim text from Katherine Pyle's 1922 English children's retelling. The collection labels it Lithuanian but does not identify an oral informant or underlying source text.

narrativeBlocks.title: The king's three sons
narrativeBlocks.body: A Lithuanian king has three sons — and a stepsister (or step-relation in the telling) who schemes against them: her malice drives the story.

narrativeBlocks.title: The stepsister's slander
narrativeBlocks.body: She poisons the father's ear — lies and forged accusations — until the king banishes his own sons: cast out to wander in the world with nothing.

narrativeBlocks.title: Into the wide world
narrativeBlocks.body: The princes go out into the world together — the exile that every fairy-tale hero begins with: home lost, road ahead, nothing but each other.

narrativeBlocks.title: The oath of the road
narrativeBlocks.body: They swear to stand by one another — the brotherhood of the road is the tale's strength, and the youngest will prove the truest.

narrativeBlocks.title: A Lithuanian-told tale
narrativeBlocks.body: This is one Lithuanian-labeled retelling in Howard Pyle's fairy-tale collection — a single tale, not a survey of all Baltic myth, and we hold it as such.
